Law Passed: Maine's packaging EPR law (LD 1541, enacted July 2021) is in active implementation. The Maine DEP issued an RFP for a Stewardship Organization on June 15, 2026, with the solicitation closing August 23, 2026 and SO contract expected to begin September 15, 2026.

Producer guidance covering who qualifies as a producer, packaging material type identification, registration, and reporting methods is set for publication in summer 2026.

Law Passed: Washington E2SSB 5284 (Recycling Reform Act, Chapter 70A.208 RCW) — signed into law May 17, 2025; active implementation underway as of August 2026, including a public comment period on preliminary statewide collection lists (Aug. 5–19, 2026).
Status Detail: The Recycling Reform Act establishes an EPR program for residential packaging (including plastic, paper, metal, and glass) and paper products, requiring producers to join the Circular Action Alliance (CAA), which was designated as the sole PRO by the Washington Department of Ecology on March 4, 2026. The July 1, 2026 deadline for producers to be registered with a PRO has now passed; Ecology is conducting a public comment period through August 19, 2026 on preliminary statewide collection lists, with final lists due by October 1, 2026. Rulemaking is ongoing, with full program implementation and PRO cost reimbursements for service providers scheduled for January 1, 2030.

Law Passed: Colorado HB22-1355 (Producer Responsibility Program for Statewide Recycling Act), signed June 3, 2022, covering all packaging materials and paper products (including poly bags, plastic film, paper, and other flexible/rigid packaging). The program entered active implementation as of January 1, 2026, with producer dues obligations live. Within the last 30 days, the ILMA lawsuit against CDPHE (filed March 12, 2026) remains pending in Denver District Court with no injunction in place, and SB26-192 (EPR dues appeal bill) was introduced in the 2026 session but did not advance to enactment before the legislature adjourned May 13, 2026.
Status Detail: Colorado's EPR program is fully live: producers of all covered packaging and paper products have been required to register with CAA since October 2024, submit supply reports (2024 data due July 31, 2025; 2025 data due May 31, 2026), and pay annual dues beginning January 2026. CDPHE approved CAA's final program plan on December 9, 2025, with CAA required to begin full implementation by June 9, 2026. A legal challenge by the Independent Lubricant Manufacturers Association (ILMA) filed March 12, 2026 in Denver District Court alleges constitutional and statutory violations in CDPHE's program implementation; no injunction has been issued and the program continues to operate.

Law Passed: Minnesota Packaging Waste and Cost Reduction Act (HF 3911 / Minn. Stat. § 115A.144–115A.1463), signed into law May 21, 2024; active implementation ongoing with MPCA rulemaking initiated May 2026.
Status Detail: The law is fully enacted and in active implementation. The MPCA completed a preliminary assessment in February 2026 and needs assessment surveys are underway with a final needs assessment due December 31, 2026. On May 15, 2026, the MPCA issued a formal notice of intent to develop rules to clarify definitions, exemptions, and statewide requirements under the Act, representing a significant recent development in implementation. Covered materials broadly include all packaging and packaging components (including plastic film such as boat wrap, single-use bags, food wrapping film, and shipping materials), food packaging, and paper products sold or shipped into Minnesota.

Law Passed: New Jersey S673 / A3744 ("Packaging and Paper Product Stewardship Act") — the 2026-session reintroduction of prior bills S3398 / A5009 — is pending in the Senate Environment and Energy Committee. No EPR packaging law has been enacted in New Jersey.
Status Detail: S3398 and A5009 died on January 12, 2026, when the 2024–2025 legislative session ended without a floor vote. The bills were reintroduced on January 13, 2026, as S673 / A3744 in the new 2026–2027 session and referred to the Senate Environment and Energy Committee, where they remain pending with no further action reported. The legislation would cover all packaging product types — including primary, secondary, tertiary, and service packaging (carry-out bags, bulk goods bags, take-out bags, home delivery packaging, etc.) — made of any material, requiring producers to join a PRO or submit their own stewardship plan and meet source-reduction and recyclability targets.

Law Passed: No packaging EPR law has passed in Connecticut. HB 6917 (2025), a feasibility study bill for consumer packaging EPR, was tabled to the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025, and did not advance to enactment. A follow-on bill, HB 5151 (2026), which would have required EPR recommendations based on Connecticut's waste characterization study, was introduced February 11, 2026, but died in committee. Connecticut is not among the seven states with enacted packaging EPR laws.
Status Detail: Connecticut's 2025 packaging EPR activity was limited to HB 6917 (Substitute), which would have mandated a study on the need and viability of packaging EPR for consumer packaging by January 15, 2027; the bill was tabled to the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025, the final day of the legislative session, and did not become law. In the 2026 session, HB 5151 was introduced to advance EPR recommendations derived from the state's waste characterization study but died in committee. Connecticut's 2026 session has concluded with no packaging EPR bill enacted, and any new bill would need to be reintroduced in 2027.

Law Passed: Georgia HB 1237, the Pollution Prevention and Producer Responsibility Act of 2026, was introduced on February 6, 2026, and died in committee without advancing.
Status Detail: HB 1237 would have amended Chapter 8 of Title 12 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated to establish a comprehensive EPR framework covering packaging, paper products, and beverage containers, with a Producer Responsibility Advisory Board, recycling and composting standards, toxin reduction requirements, and reporting and enforcement provisions. No EPR packaging law has been enacted in Georgia.

Law Passed: Missouri HB 3504, the 'Producer Responsibility Program for Statewide Recycling Act,' was introduced on February 26, 2026 and referred to the House Emerging Issues Committee on May 15, 2026. The 2026 regular session has since adjourned (sine die) without the bill advancing further.
Status Detail: HB 3504 would require producers of packaging and paper products — including all packaging material types — to join or form a nonprofit Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO) that funds and manages a statewide recycling system. The bill is a partisan Democratic-sponsored measure and did not meaningfully advance, remaining in early committee stage at adjournment. Missouri is considered a political longshot for EPR passage in the near term.

Law Passed: New Hampshire HB 1789-FN, an EPR packaging bill introduced January 7, 2026, was voted 'Inexpedient to Legislate' by the House on February 19, 2026. No EPR packaging law has passed in New Hampshire.
Status Detail: HB 1789-FN would have established a producer-funded packaging reduction and recycling program covering all packaging materials (paper, plastic, glass, metal, and multi-material), requiring producers to pay stewardship fees based on the quantity and type of packaging sold into New Hampshire. The House adopted the 'Inexpedient to Legislate' motion by voice vote on February 19, 2026, effectively killing the bill. This follows the same outcome as the prior-session bill HB 1630, which was also voted down in February 2024.

Law Passed: Tennessee SB 0269 / HB 0600 (Tennessee Waste to Jobs Act), a packaging EPR bill introduced in January 2025, was sidelined in the Senate Energy, Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee on March 11, 2026 and died when the 114th General Assembly adjourned sine die on April 23, 2026. No EPR packaging law has been enacted in Tennessee.
Status Detail: SB 0269 / HB 0600 was introduced January 23, 2025 by Sen. Heidi Campbell (D) and Rep. Sponsor Campbell has publicly committed to reintroducing the bill in the 2027 session with a more intensive public campaign.

Law Passed: Vermont S.139 (2025-2026 session), 'An act relating to the management of materials from packaging,' was introduced April 2, 2025, and referred to the Senate Committee on Natural Resources and Energy, where it did not advance out of committee.
Status Detail: S.139 would have required a needs assessment on the management of packaging materials distributed in Vermont — covering reuse, recyclability, safety, toxicity reduction, and quantity — including all packaging types such as film, bags, and other forms. The bill was referred to the Senate Committee on Natural Resources and Energy on April 2, 2025, but failed to advance out of committee by end of the 2025 portion of the session. Vermont is identified as a state that could attempt a renewed packaging EPR effort in 2027 or 2028.
